@graph.name: Casa Nina Flamingo
@graph.description: Luxury seven-bedroom villa in Playa Flamingo, Guanacaste, Costa Rica. Sleeps 14 across two independent living units, with a private elevator, concierge service and included airport transfers.

@graph.name: Frequently Asked Questions | Casa Nina Flamingo
@graph.description: Answers about booking, deposits, airport transfers, included services, private chef options, pool safety and Wi-Fi at Casa Nina Flamingo, a 7-bedroom villa in Playa Flamingo, Costa Rica.

mainEntity.name: How do I reserve Casa Nina?

acceptedAnswer.text: There are two ways to reserve. Send an inquiry through our availability form and a member of our team will reply to you personally, or book instantly through our Airbnb listing. Booking directly connects you with the people who care for the villa every day, and it is always where you will find our best rates.

mainEntity.name: What deposit is required, and when is the balance due?

acceptedAnswer.text: A deposit of 50% of your total secures your dates, with the balance due 14 days before arrival. We accept payment by credit card. Both payments are set out in your booking summary, so the numbers are never a surprise.

mainEntity.name: What is the cancellation policy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Full refund up to 30 days before arrival; no refund inside 30 days. For stays over Christmas, New Year's, March Break and Easter: full refund up to 60 days before arrival, 50% up to 30 days, and no refund inside 30 days. If you are considering travel insurance, or think your dates might move, mention it to our concierge before you book and they will walk you through your options.

mainEntity.name: Is there a security deposit?

acceptedAnswer.text: A refundable damage hold is placed on your credit card: $2,500 for the Full Casa and $1,500 for the Half Casa, released after your stay. The hold is set out clearly in your booking summary before you pay, so there are no surprises when you arrive.

mainEntity.name: Is there a minimum stay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Casa Nina has a 4-night minimum stay. Over the festive weeks of Christmas, New Year's, March Break and Easter, the minimum is 7 nights. Share your dates with us and we will confirm availability right away.

mainEntity.name: If we book the Half Casa, do we have to share the pool and patio space?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, never. The Half Casa is a private three-bedroom home with its own kitchen, living space and laundry. When you reserve it, you will have exclusive, private access to the pool and patio and it is never shared with anyone else. The main residence upstairs is never rented alongside the Half Casa. On occasion the owners’ family may be staying there, and the pool and patio remain exclusively yours and never shared.

mainEntity.name: What are check-in and check-out times?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check-in is from 3:00 PM and check-out is by 10:00 AM. Our concierge coordinates your exact arrival over WhatsApp, so everything is ready when you walk in.

mainEntity.name: How far is the airport, and is transportation included?

acceptedAnswer.text: Casa Nina is about an hour by road from Liberia Guanacaste International Airport (LIR), and private airport pick-up and drop-off are included with every stay. Your driver will be waiting for you at arrivals. If you are flying into San José (SJO) instead, plan for roughly four hours by road. We will gladly arrange that transfer as well.

mainEntity.name: Can we arrange early check-in or late check-out?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early check-in is often possible when the villa is ready, and we are always happy to hold your luggage while it is being prepared. Late check-out works whenever there is no same-day turnover. Share your flight times when you book and our team will build the day around them.

mainEntity.name: Do we need a rental car?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many of our guests find a car is not needed, however, a golf cart is usually recommended at the least. The beach is a short walk away, airport transfers are included, and our concierge can arrange drivers for dinners and day trips. If you would like your own transport, we can arrange a rental car, in all different sizes, or an electric golf cart (4 or 6 passenger), which is welcome on all local roads and a favorite way to get around Flamingo or surrounding towns to restaurants and beaches.

mainEntity.name: How many guests does Casa Nina sleep?

acceptedAnswer.text: Casa Nina sleeps fourteen guests across seven bedrooms and six bathrooms, with two independent living units, dual kitchens and a private elevator connecting the floors. It is one of the very few villas in Playa Flamingo where a whole multigenerational family can gather without anyone compromising on comfort.

mainEntity.name: What does “two independent living units” mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: Casa Nina is designed as two self-contained homes under one roof: the main residence and a three-bedroom unit (the Half Casa), each with its own kitchen and living areas. Book the full villa and use the separation however suits your group: grandparents and early bedtimes on one side, the night owls on the other.

mainEntity.name: Is there an elevator? How accessible is the villa?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, fully. A ramp at the entrance, a private elevator serving all three floors, and curbless walk-in showers make Casa Nina genuinely wheelchair accessible, a rare comfort in Playa Flamingo. The layout also makes life easier for grandparents and for parents carrying a sleeping toddler up to bed. If access matters to your group, share your needs with our concierge and they will confirm every detail personally.

mainEntity.name: How close is the beach?

acceptedAnswer.text: Playa Flamingo's white sand is a short, less than a 10-min walk from the villa, close enough to wander back whenever you please. We can also arrange beach packages with tents, chairs, food and drinks, so your spot is set up before you stroll down.

mainEntity.name: What are the bed configurations?

acceptedAnswer.text: Seven bedrooms, every one with an ocean view: Bedroom 1 (Floor 1, Half or Full Casa): king bed, ensuite bathroom, walk-in closet; Bedroom 2 (Floor 1, Half or Full Casa): queen bed, shared bathroom; Bedroom 3 (Floor 1, Half or Full Casa): king bed, shared bathroom; Bedroom 4 (Floor 2, Full Casa): king bed, ensuite bathroom, walk-in closet; Bedroom 5 (Floor 2, Full Casa): queen bed, shared bathroom; Bedroom 6 (Floor 2, Full Casa): king bed, shared bathroom; Bedroom 7 (Floor 3, Full Casa): king bed, ensuite bathroom. A crib is available in Bedroom 1, and if you are traveling with little ones or have particular room requests, our concierge will plan the rooms with you before you arrive.

mainEntity.name: Is there air conditioning and laundry?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every bedroom, living room and kitchen has its own A/C unit, and the first and second floors each have a dedicated laundry room with a washer and dryer. Our concierge team can confirm any other comfort question within minutes.

mainEntity.name: What are the house rules on pets and smoking?

acceptedAnswer.text: The house keeps two simple rules: no smoking indoors, and no pets. Whatever you are dreaming up, from a birthday dinner to a sunrise yoga circle, share it with our concierge and they will tell you exactly what is possible.

mainEntity.name: What's included with every stay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every booking includes a dedicated concierge service, private airport pick-up and drop-off, daily maid and turnover service, and a private chef for two breakfasts. You pay only the cost of the food. Few villas include all of this as standard. Here, it is simply how your stay begins.

mainEntity.name: Who looks after us during our stay?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your host and concierge team, your single point of contact from booking to checkout. They will set up a WhatsApp group for your stay, coordinate your arrival, and arrange anything from a chef dinner to a catamaran day. Our hosts are mentioned by name in guest reviews, and once you have been welcomed in, you will understand why.

mainEntity.name: How does daily housekeeping work?

acceptedAnswer.text: The villa is refreshed daily by our maid service, included with every stay. Additional cleaning or mid-stay turnovers can be arranged whenever you'd like them. Our team will arrange timing around your group's rhythm, whether that means a slow breakfast or an early start at the beach.

mainEntity.name: How do the included chef breakfasts work?

acceptedAnswer.text: A private chef prepares breakfast for your group on two mornings of your stay. It's included with every booking, and guests cover only the cost of the ingredients. There is no better way to begin a villa morning: everyone around one table while the kitchen is taken care of. If you would like more mornings, or lunches and dinners as well, you will find everything in the chef and dining answers below.

mainEntity.name: Can we book a private chef for lunch and dinner?

acceptedAnswer.text: With pleasure. Chef Rafael cooks at Casa Nina by arrangement, and his current experiences include: Costa Rican menu: $60 to $70 per person; Surf & Turf Experience: $80 per person (minimum 6 guests); Fish Night: $75 per person (minimum 6 guests); Craft Burger night: $55 per person, with Japanese Wagyu upgrades available; Taco Bar: $55 per person (minimum 6, buffet style). Prices and menus are set by the chef and may evolve with the seasons. Our concierge will share the latest and reserve your evenings before you arrive.

mainEntity.name: How does grocery delivery work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Send us your list and we will have everything stocked before you walk in: fridge, pantry and cold drinks. The service is a flat $50 fee plus the cost of your groceries. We can share a suggested starter list with breakfast basics, snacks and the makings of a spaghetti night, or shop to exactly what your group loves.

mainEntity.name: What are the kitchens like?

acceptedAnswer.text: There are two full kitchens, one in each living unit, so even a large group has all the room it needs. Cook together one night and invite Chef Rafael in the next. Each kitchen is fully equipped: fridge with ice maker, stove, oven, dishwasher, coffee machine, blender, toaster, and every plate, pot, pan and utensil a group of fourteen could need. You will also find barbecues on the first-floor patio and the rooftop terrace.

mainEntity.name: Can the chef handle dietary restrictions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, of course. Tell our concierge about any allergies, vegetarian preferences or children's plates when you book your chef experiences, and they will coordinate everything with the chef directly. Buffet-style experiences like the Taco Bar are wonderful for groups with mixed tastes, since everyone composes their own plate.

mainEntity.name: Is the pool safe for young children?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with the usual care around water. The infinity pool is 5 feet deep with easy-access steps, and a fully secured railing runs along the perimeter of the terrace. Please ask our concierge anything at all. Every question is answered fully before you book.

mainEntity.name: Is the pool heated?

acceptedAnswer.text: The pool is unheated because it simply does not need it: the water typically sits around 75 to 80 degrees. Guanacaste is Costa Rica's warmest, sunniest coast, and most of the year here is pool weather.

mainEntity.name: Is the villa gated or secured?

acceptedAnswer.text: The neighborhood is protected by full 24/7 security, with monitored cameras along the streets and around the perimeter of the house, and a dedicated guard stationed outside the villa gate from 6 PM to 6 AM. Our house team is at the villa daily, the concierge is only a WhatsApp message away, and any concern is met with a quick, personal response.

mainEntity.name: What about medical care nearby?

acceptedAnswer.text: Several clinics and pharmacies are close by, the nearest at the Flamingo Marina less than a five-minute drive away, with professional doctors, a full pharmacy, an ambulance and even a heliport for emergencies. Every emergency contact number is in your guest guide, and our concierge team will always help you reach the right care quickly.

mainEntity.name: How fast is the Wi-Fi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fast on every floor. Each level has its own dedicated modem, with measured speeds of 278 Mbps down and 52 Mbps up in the main living areas, and 113 Mbps down and 79 Mbps up in the farthest bedroom. If your stay depends on a particular speed, for video calls or a working holiday, our concierge can run a fresh speed test for you before you book.

mainEntity.name: Is there space to work?

acceptedAnswer.text: With two living units, seven bedrooms and several living areas, there is always a quiet corner to work from. The third-floor bedroom has a dedicated work desk and chair, and the large dining tables on the first and second floors make generous work-friendly spots.

mainEntity.name: What is cell coverage like?

acceptedAnswer.text: All local carriers work very well at the house, with Liberty and ICE the two you will typically see. Major Costa Rican carriers cover Playa Flamingo well, most international phones roam smoothly, and eSIM data plans are an easy, affordable option for the week.

mainEntity.name: What is there to do near the villa?

acceptedAnswer.text: On the water: surf classes, kayaking and stand-up paddle, snorkeling and scuba, guided fishing charters, and all-inclusive catamaran days with open bar and lunch. On land: horseback riding through mountains and along beaches, ATV and UTV tours, mountain biking, canopy zip-lining, or an at-home spa day with massages, facials and mani-pedis at the villa or on the beach. Our concierge will happily arrange all of it.

mainEntity.name: Which full-day tours do guests love?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our guests return to three again and again. The Vandara Explorer Pass: thermal hot springs, mineral mud baths, hanging bridges and jungle water slides on a rainforest property beside Rincón de la Vieja National Park. The Diamante Adventure Pass: the country's longest, most scenic zipline, plus an animal sanctuary, botanical gardens and Hammock Beach. And the Palo Verde river tour: crocodiles, white-faced monkeys and some of the park's 280+ bird species in a wetland of international importance.

mainEntity.name: Can we go further afield, like Arenal or Monteverde?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gladly. Multi-day journeys are part of what our concierge arranges. Arenal and La Fortuna: volcano hikes, La Fortuna Waterfall, hanging bridges and hot springs, with an eco-resort stay at Hotel Montaña de Fuego. Monteverde: the cloud forest's treetop walkways, butterfly gardens and Selvatura Park, with lunch and transport taken care of. Share your dates with our concierge and they will build the itinerary around them.

mainEntity.name: Can we host a wedding, retreat or event?

acceptedAnswer.text: The villa hosts retreat-sized groups by design, with two living units, dual kitchens and room for fourteen overnight. Special events and celebrations are warmly welcomed as long as they are organized through our management team, with no extra fees or deposit required. If you are planning one, start the conversation early and we will plan it properly with you.

mainEntity.name: Where exactly is Playa Flamingo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Playa Flamingo sits on Costa Rica's Gold Coast in Guanacaste province: a white-sand beach town on the northern Pacific, about an hour from Liberia International Airport (LIR). Flamingo pairs a genuinely beautiful beach with everything close at hand: restaurants, a marina, and day trips in every direction.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to visit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dry season runs roughly December through April, with reliable sun and long blue days. Green season, May through November, trades a brief afternoon shower for lush green hills, fewer crowds and gentler rates. Many of our guests call it their favorite secret. There is no bad month here, only different moods.

mainEntity.name: What currency should we bring? Do people tip?

acceptedAnswer.text: Costa Rica uses the colón, but US dollars are accepted almost everywhere in Guanacaste and cards are widely taken. Restaurants add a 10% service charge by law. Rounding up for great service, and for your guides and drivers, is appreciated but never expected.

mainEntity.name: Is the tap water safe? What language is spoken?

acceptedAnswer.text: Costa Rican tap water is generally safe to drink, and bottled water is easy to stock through our grocery delivery if you prefer it. Spanish is the local language, English is spoken widely across the area, and our team is happy to host you in English every day.
